chapter: Piano influences: Teddy Wilson, Tatum and Bud Powell
title: The Benny Goodman Trio and eight years modeled on Teddy Wilson
summary: Hearing China Boy on the radio seals his devotion to Teddy Wilson's style, including the left-hand tenths.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Anyway, while we were sitting there talking... Oh, I told him, I said, "This guy plays pretty piano, but it's kind of in a slow vein..." I didn't know to use the term (?) or whatever. But I said I didn't think he could play very fast, like a lot of things that Earl Hines does.

So while we were talking about this, on the radio in one of the afternoon programs (I wouldn't have no idea whose program it was) came this record of an old tune called "China Boy." And it turned out to be the Benny Goodman Trio. And the guy said later it was Teddy Wilson, Benny Goodman and Gene Krupa. And that really blew my mind. So for I guess the next... That was 1936. Probably for the next eight years, my whole thing was wrapped up in Teddy Wilson, with maybe little sprinkles of a run or something from Art Tatum that I could find or that someone would show me. Billy Taylor and I used to sit and listen to Art Tatum a lot, and we'd try to catch runs and things. But basically, the style that I was trying to play was Teddy Wilson. And he also had a way of playing his left hand which involved tenths in his left hand that I
hadn't heard anyone do like the way he did before.
